title: This Moth Breaks Into Beehives, Squeaks, and Steals the Honey

scenes.text: It's a death's-head hawkmoth, with a wingspan up to five inches.
Its scent helps it slip past the guard bees.
Once inside, it squeaks, and scientists still debate why.
A short, tough proboscis lets it suck up the honey.
The guards barely resist. The thief takes the honey and leaves.

description:
The death's-head hawkmoth breaks into beehives to steal honey.
Its wingspan can reach five inches, its scent helps it past the guards, and it squeaks while it raids.
Would you let this moth near your hive?
first_comment: Why do you think the moth squeaks?
